svg.title: More than one card
svg.text: two cards, one run: ranks go on across the cards
km.Session(cards=[0, 1]); run.submit("map", (96, 44)): one command, its group in flat ranks
its part, to its own dispatcher
the group here, ranks 96 to 117: cores 96 to 117
its part, to its own dispatcher
the group here, ranks 118 to 139: cores 0 to 21
a command's part, ask and put lines, in order
a page a packet, into DRAM or a core's L1
L0, L1: link cores, not ranks; each data-movement CPU holds a link
a group is (first, count), anywhere in the flat ranks
Ran: two P150A joined by four links, and one card split into two to four islands joined in each of the first five ways.
islands are a graph; a rank may be any number of links away

svg.text: The four measured across two cards; the three times on one card split as a line of three, for 16 bytes and an add.
the link cores serve four operations, by flat rank or by tensor page
each core asks the island that holds its pages
a hint puts each part on its ranks' island
a kernel runs unchanged; a program that knows its islands crosses less

svg.text: session.tensor(data, dtype, layout, split=, group=, like=, copy=)
The hint says how the program uses the tensor, in the kernel's words; the session decides which island holds which page.

svg.text: km::write_pages(writer, command, state, page, 1, scratch) && writes_done()
On one island each call is the local page read or write. Over islands a core reads the pages its island holds from its own DRAM;
each run of pages another island holds is one line across, an ask or a put, waited for at the core's port. The kernel is the same.
a tensor is placed by a hint, and a kernel names the tensor, never the island

svg.text: a reduce or broadcast inside this island
the first rank of each island's part
one part to a rank of island i
the group; its first rank; a local send
a kernel may act by island, in its own words
Ranks are flat and contiguous by island. Between two cards a link runs through the router on an Ethernet tile of each card (row 1 of the
grid); on a split card it is a write over the card's own NoC. Every number is a run on two P150A joined by four links, or on a split card where said.
